title: Home & Daily Life
description: Around the house: the kitchen and the bathroom, the chores, the power and the neighbours.

items.registerNotes: In speech the root: cuci tangan (wash your hands), cuci piring (do the dishes), cuci baju (do the laundry). Written mencuci.
items.pitfallNote: Washing yourself all over is mandi. You cuci your hands, face, clothes and dishes.

items.registerNotes: Written memasak. Masakan is cooking or a dish: masakan Padang (Padang food).

items.english: to clean up, do the cleaning
items.registerNotes: The everyday way to say you're cleaning: Saya sedang bersih-bersih rumah. To clean one thing, use bersihkan: Tolong bersihkan mejanya.
At a hotel: Boleh minta handuk lagi? (Could I have another towel?)

items.cultureNote: Many bathrooms have a water tank (bak mandi) and a gayung: you scoop water and pour it over yourself, and never climb into the tank. By the toilet, a gayung or a hose takes the place of paper.

items.registerNotes: Kamarnya dingin, boleh minta selimut? (The room's cold. Could I have a blanket?)

items.cultureNote: Many homes and rented rooms have prepaid meters: you buy a token (token listrik) at a minimarket or in an app and key in the code.

items.registerNotes: Tolong matikan lampunya (please turn the light off). Lampu merah, literally red light, is a set of traffic lights, a common landmark in directions.
Literally wind fan. Kipas on its own is any fan, including a hand fan.
Said a se. Rooms are often offered as AC or non-AC. Bisa nyalakan AC-nya? (Could you turn the air-con on?)
Buang sampah is to throw rubbish away, and a bin is a tempat sampah. Signs say Buanglah sampah pada tempatnya (put rubbish in its place).

items.cultureNote: Neighbours greet you in passing with Mau ke mana? or Dari mana? It's a friendly hello, and a vague answer such as Jalan-jalan is enough.

items.registerNotes: Includes the everyday food shopping: belanja ke pasar (going to the market for groceries). Written berbelanja.
To sweep is menyapu, or nyapu in casual speech.
From Portuguese janela. Boleh buka jendelanya? (May I open the window?)
Atapnya bocor (the roof leaks) is a common rainy-season complaint.
